name: Noa Koren
bio:
Noa came to the studio from the Tel Aviv nightlife circuit — not as a fixture, but as someone who already understood how a room changes when the lights drop. She works slowly. She holds a look a beat longer than expected.

On set she is the calm center: precise with marks, generous with scene partners, and unusually comfortable in long, quiet takes. Directors keep writing her into the openings of features because the camera settles when she does.

Off camera she still lives by the sea. Most of her stills for the house lookbook were shot in late afternoon, when the city turns copper.

name: Yael Dahan
tagline: Sharp lines. A colder kind of heat.
bio:
Yael is the studio's most architectural presence — cropped silhouette, measured walk, a face the lens reads as editorial before it reads as intimate. She trained in movement before she ever stood in front of a production camera.

Haifa gave her a taste for contrast: industrial edges against the water. That contrast is the reason we signed her. She does not decorate a frame. She divides it.

Her first house productions leaned into tailored wardrobe and withheld dialogue. The work is cooler than the rest of the slate, and that is the point.

name: Liora Sasson
bio:
Liora is the house's night performer. She prefers practicals to studio key lights and will ask to keep a room one stop darker than the meter wants. The result is always more expensive-looking than the budget.

She grew up around stone and stairs and late conversations. That density shows up in her pacing: she does not rush a scene, and she does not fill silence with business.

When we need a feature that feels like a closed door instead of a spectacle, we start with Liora.

name: Eden Barak
tagline: Desert gold and an open face.
bio:
Eden is the newest Israeli signature on the roster and already the most photographed in natural light. She brings a sun-struck, unguarded quality that the rest of the slate does not have.

We found her through a stills test in the south — no dialogue, just wind and a linen shirt. The contact sheet was enough. She signed the following week.

On a feature set she is still learning the machinery and already ignoring the parts that do not serve the shot. That is a good instinct.

name: Sofia Renard
bio:
Sofia is the studio's European center of gravity. She arrived from Lyon with a modeling book and a refusal to play 'available.' We built a lane around that refusal.

Her scenes are composed like stills that happen to move. She understands wardrobe as architecture and treats a silk blouse like a lighting instrument.

When a production needs to feel imported — a hotel, a train, a city that is not ours — Sofia is the first call.

name: Isla Meridian
tagline: Atlantic weather in a warm room.
bio:
Isla brings weather into the frame. Even under tungsten she looks like she just came in from rain. That softness is not vagueness — it is control.

She works best opposite stronger, colder scene partners. The contrast writes itself. Directors have started asking for her specifically when a picture needs a pulse under the gloss.

Between productions she stays in London and treats the house like a visiting company, not a hometown.

name: Carmen Soler
bio:
Carmen is the studio's most dangerous smile. She can turn a two-shot into a chase without standing up. We keep her for the pictures that need appetite more than atmosphere.

Valencia is still in her voice. She refuses to flatten it for English-language productions, and the sound mix is better for it.

On set she is exacting about jewelry, lipstick, and when a scene should stop talking. Producers learned to listen.

name: Anya Petrov
bio:
Anya photographs like a still from a colder film. Pale, precise, slightly removed. She is the reason we started booking winter interiors on purpose.

Prague is both her home and her set language: corridors, glass, a kind of formal distance that makes closeness land harder when it arrives.

She is not the house's warmest performer. She is one of its most watched.

name: Amara Cole
bio:
Amara came from fashion before she came to us, and she never dropped the discipline. Every angle is a decision. Every still looks like a campaign.

She is the performer other performers watch in video village. Presence like that is not taught; it is edited around.

We keep her on the flagship slate — the pictures that have to introduce the house to someone who has never heard the name.

name: Elise Moreau
bio:
Elise is the studio's North American winter. She works in a lower register — almost conversational — and then the scene tightens without anyone raising their voice.

Montreal gave her two languages and a habit of underplaying. On an international slate that reads as expensive.

She is still early in her house run. The stills already argue for more features.
